newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Six main U.N. Assembly committees elect chairmen.
newsitem.headline: Six main U.N. Assembly committees elect chairmen.

text.p: Diplomats from Belarus, Netherlands, Mexico, Laos, Zimbabwe and Venezuela were elected by acclamation on Tuesday as chairmen of the U.N. General Assembly's main committees.
All were the unopposed candidates of their respective regional groups.
Those elections followed the election by acclamation of Malaysian U.N. embassador Razali Ismail as president of the 185-nation Assembly on the session's opening day.
Alyaksandr Sychou, the permanent representative of Belarus, was chosen chairman of the Assembly's disarmament and international security (first) committee.
Arjan Hamburger, minister in charge of economic affairs at the Netherlands U.N. mission, became chairman of the economic and financial (second) committee.
Patricia Espinosa, minister responsible for human rights and social affairs in Mexico's U.N. mission, was elected chairman of the social, humanitarian and cultural (third) committee.
Elected to head the special political and decolonization (fourth) committee was Alounkeo Kittikhoun, Laos's permanent U.N. envoy.

Ngoni Francis Sengwe, Zimbabwe's deputy permanent U.N. representative, heads the administrative and budgetary (fifth) committee, while Ramon Escovar Salom, Venezuela's new permanent representative and a former interior minister, chairs the legal (sixth) committee.

Elected without opposition as the 21 vice-presidents of the Assembly -- positions held by countries rather than individuals -- were Andorra, Angola, Bahamas, Burundi, China, Cyprus, France, Ghana, Honduras, Latvia, Libya, Niger, Pakistan, Paraguay, Philippines, Russia, Sudan, Turkey, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom and the United States.
